text.tspan: vSphere Client: Cluster → Monitor → vSAN → Skyline
Health
Check failed health checks and recommended actions
esxcli vsan debug object list on ESXi
Filter: grep -v Healthy to find problem objects
vSphere Client: Monitor → vSAN → Performance
Check cluster read/write latency and congestion
esxcli vsan cluster unicastagent list
vmkping -I vmk2 -d -s 8972 peer-vmk-ip
esxcli vsan storage list
esxcli storage core device smart get -d naa
grep LSOM vmkernel.log
esxcli vsan debug resync summary get
Check slack space and bandwidth cap settings
Follow recommended action in Skyline Health UI
Re-run health check to confirm fix
Step 2: object-level diagnostics
esxcli vsan debug object list
esxcli vsan debug object list -u uuid
Check component locations and health state
esxcli vsan perf get
Identify noisy VM: PowerCLI Get-Stat disk.write.average
esxcli vsan network list
esxcli network nic stats get -n vmnic2
Check SMART: Reallocated Pending Uncorrectable sectors
grep naa.device vmkernel.log for errors
Check slack space: esxcli vsan storage list
Review resync bandwidth: vSAN config
Collect vCenter and ESXi support bundle
Open VMware SR
vc-support.sh from VCSA + vm-support --vsan on
each ESXi host
Attach to VMware Support Request
